text:
Anna: quick heads-up — ran a 1k-request latency sweep across AWS p4d (a100), GCP a2-highgpu-1g, and Azure NDv4 using the same model + CUDA 12.1 driver. seeing consistent median parity but tails diverge: GCP tails ~35% higher than AWS, Azure ~18% higher.

Rohit: ouch. same kernel/cudnn? any cuBLAS fallbacks?

Anna: same driver bundle (NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-525.105.17) and cuDNN 8.6 pinned. no obvious cuBLAS error in logs, but profiler shows extra memcpy stalls on GCP for sequence lengths >1024.

Marta: memcpy stalls could be NUMA/cpu governor related. what instance physical topology did you use on GCP?

Anna: GCP was a2-highgpu-1g (1 GPU) on N2 machine type. AWS p4d is dense node (8xA100) but we ran in 1-GPU partition via MIG disabled for parity. Azure NDv4 was 1xA100VM.

benchmark-bot: automated-run: infra/bench/sweep_v2.sh --model=gpt-small --seq=2048 --iters=1000 --batch=1 --out=/tmp/bench/1748004321.csv

Rohit: can you paste the relevant wall-clock latency percentile numbers?

Anna: pastebin: https://console.redwood/internal/bench/1748004321 (private). quick excerpt: AWS p50 28ms p95 42ms p99 58ms; GCP p50 29ms p95 57ms p99 79ms; AZ p50 30ms p95 50ms p99 69ms.

Marta: interesting that medians are close but p95/p99 diverge. suggests transient kernel scheduling or PCIe DMA contention. did you enable tsched for the kernel?

Anna: kernels are stock from images: AWS deep-learning ami (5.10), GCP cos/ubuntu 5.15 guest, AZ 5.11.

Rohit: different host kernels + iommu/pcie_aspm defaults could impact memcpy latencies. also check nv_peer_mem + GPU direct RDMA settings.

Anna: good call. i ran nvidia-smi topo -m and dmesg grep -i nvidia; no RDMA set. copying full prof dump: ```
GPU memcpy H2D avg 0.42ms | H2D tail spikes on GCP up to 6.3ms | stream::cutlass matmul avg 12ms p99 18ms (aws)
nvlink: none on these single-gpu VMs
cpu governor: GCP shows ondemand, AWS shows performance
```

Marta: CPU governor difference alone can cause jitter if host-side memcpy threads are starved. set governor to performance and re-run with isolation (cpuset) on GCP for reproducer.

Anna: I'll run a control: GCP with governor=performance, disable hyperthreading, and a pinned cpuset for the memcpy threads. will post results in ~30m.

Rohit: also try switching CUDA kernel selector envs: TF_CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG / CUTLASS heuristics? for our runtime, try env REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=prefer_cutlass vs prefer_cublas — might change kernel shapes + memcpy patterns.

Anna: good idea. one more hypothesis: quantization run we did last week (int8) reduced compute, moved bottleneck to host memcpy/copy_back, which amplifies any host-side variance. repro test will include both fp16 and int8 profiles.

benchmark-bot: queued job 1748004321-ctrl with tags [governor=performance,cpu_iso=1,env=prefer_cutlass]. ETA 25m.

Marta: i'll check kernel module params: page allocator, vm.zone_reclaim, and tcp offloads. on azure we had tuned vm.zone_reclaim=0 which helped a similar tail last quarter.

Anna: updated results (quick): GCP control: p50 29ms p95 44ms p99 61ms. improvement but still ~5-10% worse than AWS p99. int8 run on GCP shows p99 95ms before change -> 68ms after governor/perf.

Rohit: much better. still odd there's residual delta. can you run ncu on the long tail requests to capture SM utilization and PCIe stalls?

Anna: scheduled ncu capture for 50 p99 samples. output will be attached to the bench run.

Marta: FYI I dug into host BIOS lists for the GCP zone we used — some have C-states aggressive defaults that coexist poorly with ondemand. will open infra ticket to request performance BIOS for experiment nodes.

Anna: plan summary: 1) repro script + governor/perf verified reduces tail on GCP but not fully equal. 2) next step ncu traces on p99s to identify whether memcpy stalls or kernel kernel (warps) divergence cause remaining gap. 3) if host still differs, we escalate to provider with perf artifacts.

Rohit: assign: @anna attach ncu traces to the ticket; @marta open infra ticket w/ BIOS & kernel params for GCP; i'll try the prefer_cutlass vs prefer_cublas sweep tomorrow and check if cuBLAS fallback patterns differ.

Anna: ack. will drop the raw traces + csv to https://console.redwood/internal/bench/1748004321/artifacts and ping when done :mag: :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident-checklist: no user-facing incidents; ticket created ENG-ML-4927 for cross-provider tail regression investigation.
